requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every question is numbered and every command line in section 3 names the question it answers and its action class.
Verify every referent as you write it: every section number, clause id and file path you cite must exist at origin/main HEAD -- open the file and check.
The status block says DRAFT -- MEASUREMENT BRIEF and states plainly that it authorizes nothing and approves no command.
If 13F, 13E, C4 or the discovery handover disagree with each other within this scope, report it in the document's own open-items section and raise a RELAY_QUESTION; never reconcile silently.
The document must be usable by a security expert at a terminal: plain command lines, no build steps, no code.
risks: Turning the brief into a capability specification or a gate document -- it is neither; it is the question set that precedes both.
Copying the Python collector's command ladders as the measured truth instead of asking whether each form works on this estate.
Asking for output to be pasted back rather than asking for field names, shapes and counts.
Forgetting the cluster virtual address question, which 13F section 5 makes load-bearing (collected as data, never a connection target).
Assuming the VSX context behaves like the discovery-side domain context; they are different mechanisms on different planes.

in: Section 1: scope and authority -- what this brief is for, that it authorizes nothing, and the exact boundary 13F section 6 draws for Check Point (device-facing SSH reads only, no write of any class, no management-server-mediated execution, no script upload).

Section 2: the question set, grouped by what the collection contract must be able to state, each question phrased so the answer is a fact about observed behaviour and not an opinion. At minimum: (a) which shell a validated administrator lands in and whether the reads need explicit clish invocation (AGENTS.md Check Point section); (b) which command reports software version, and whether its output differs between the forms; (c) which command carries the serial and the hardware model, and whether both appear in one read; (d) which command reports HA/cluster role and what its vocabulary is on a standalone device versus a member; (e) which command enumerates interfaces WITH every address on them, including the cluster virtual address, and how a virtual address is distinguished from a member's own address in that output; (f) which command prints the routing table and whether it needs a wider table selector; (g) what the configuration read is called, whether it needs a raised timeout, and what a successful output's canonical shape is; (h) for VSX: how a virtual system context is entered, whether the context survives across commands on one channel or must be re-entered per command, and which of (b) to (g) change per virtual system; (i) whether any of these reads can return output that carries a credential, key or other secret; (j) how command completion is signalled -- exit status, prompt, or neither -- for each read.

Section 3: the exact command sequence the Product Owner runs, ordered, numbered, each line runnable as typed with placeholders for estate values, each annotated with the question it answers and with 'read-only, class 0' or a stop. Include, for each command, what the Product Owner should RECORD: field or column names, output shape, line counts, whether an absent value is a placeholder or a dropped column -- counts and shapes only, per AGENTS.md sensitive identity reporting law, with an explicit reminder at the top of the section that no address, hostname, serial or configuration line is to be pasted back.

Section 4: what must be recorded about the configuration read specifically, because 13F section 3 requires one read and two outputs: the size of a typical output, whether it is stable across two consecutive reads of an unchanged device (the digest question), and which kinds of lines would have to be removed for the sanitized view copy -- described by category, never by example.

Section 5: the same for one VSX host with one virtual system, kept separate because 13F section 4 requires per-virtual-system inventory and the context mechanism is the part most likely to behave differently from expectation.

Section 6: what the brief deliberately does NOT ask, with the reason -- no write of any class, no policy operation, no backup command (C7 owns that), no failover-readiness battery (its own gate row), no Panorama or Palo Alto question, and no command whose purpose is to test reachability rather than to read a fact.

Section 7: the acceptance shape of the answer -- what a complete measurement record looks like when the Product Owner has run the list, so the follow-on findings document and the collection contract have a fixed target (mirror the discovery handover's structure: method table, command forms, field behaviour table, open verification items).

Add one backlog item for the follow-on work (the Check Point collection contract, blocked on this measurement) through scripts/project_queue.py -- never hand-edit project/*.json. Do not touch CURRENT_STATE.md. Commit early and often.
out: Any implementation, code, schema, screen or capability specification. Any command gate entry (the brief names commands as candidates to measure; approval is a separate act).
Running any command anywhere; contacting any device or management server.
Palo Alto in any form; backup and restore commands (C7); failover readiness commands; any write of any class; any policy operation.
Editing any FROZEN document, or applying a status to any document.

Porting or restating the existing Python collector's command list as the answer: it is know-how, and where a form from it is worth measuring, the brief asks the question rather than assuming the answer.
Any address, hostname, domain, serial, certificate subject or configuration line anywhere in the document.
